title: Service contract playbook: SLOs, error budgets, and conditional rollout policy
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Purpose: produce an operational playbook and PRD that defines standard SLOs/SLA targets, precise SLI measurement rules, error budget policies, and conditional rollout gates across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. This ticket is the product spec and acceptance criteria that engineering and SRE will use to implement SLO evaluation, alerting, and release gating logic used by the Console rollout tooling.

Scope (in):
- Define canonical SLIs for availability and latency for text generation, streaming responses, and embedding endpoints.
- Define SLO targets and error budget windows for three customer tiers (self-serve/hosted, reserved/dedicated, private on-prem).
- Specify exact measurement rules (aggregation windows, sampling, exclusion rules for maintenance windows and controlled degradation).
- Define automated and manual rollout gates (preflight checks, canary percentages with burn-rate checks, automated rollback thresholds).
- Acceptance criteria and tests (synthetic canary test plan, dashboards, alerting runbooks).

Out of scope (for this ticket):
- Implementation of the backend evaluation engine (ENG ownership).
- Billing or SLA legal contract wording (legal will consume outputs but not authored here).
- Region-by-region capacity planning knobs beyond high-level thresholds.
slo_definitions: Hosted API (self-serve): Availability SLO = 99.9% over 30d window measured as successful response rate (2xx and valid streaming chunks) excluding scheduled maintenance windows. Latency SLOs: p50 < 80ms, p95 < 350ms for short prompt workloads (<= 512 tokens); p95 < 700ms for long-tail (512-2048). Error budget = 0.1% over 30d.

Dedicated (reserved capacity): Availability SLO = 99.95% over 30d window. Latency SLOs: p50 < 60ms, p95 < 250ms (short), p95 < 600ms (long). Error budget = 0.05% over 30d. Dedicated SLOs apply per-customer pool aggregated across the pool's serving nodes.

Private (VPC / on-prem): Operational target (not contract SLA) - Availability target 99.8% over 30d. Latency guidance: p95 < 400ms (short), p95 < 900ms (long). Error budget guidance provided for customers; final contractual SLA negotiated per deployment.
sli_measurement_rules: Availability SLI: numerator = count of requests with final response code 2xx OR successful stream completion event; denominator = total requests accepted by gateway. Exclude requests with client-side validation failures (4xx) from denominator for availability SLI only.

Latency SLI: compute end-to-end server processing time measured at ingress proxy to egress of final token generation. Use request-level percentiles computed on a rolling minute-sampled window and aggregated to day/30-day windows using weighted quantile approximation (hdr histogram or t-digest as implemented by monitoring backend).
Windowing: primary SLO window = 30d rolling. Short-term gates use 24h and 1h windows for burn-rate and canary checks.

Maintenance and planned degradations: any windows announced >24h in advance and recorded in the maintenance calendar are excluded from SLI calculations for their duration. Emergency maintenance >1h must be documented within 48h to be eligible for exclusion.
rollout_gates: Preflight: synthetic smoke test must pass for 30 minutes against the exact build and runtime config in the target region. Required checks: 95% of synthetic requests within p95 latency gate for target tier, zero increased error rate vs baseline.

Canary phase 1 (1% traffic, 30m): auto-abort if error rate exceeds baseline by 3x AND absolute error rate > 0.2% OR latency p95 > 2x SLO. Also abort if error-budget burn-rate over past 10m > 5x expected burn (see burn-rate rules).

Canary phase 2 (10% traffic, 60m): proceed only if phase 1 passed. Abort if any of: 10-minute error-budget burn-rate > 3x, p95 latency > 1.5x SLO, or customer-impacting errors observed in error dashboards. Manual review required if any minor deviations are present.

Gradual rollout (10% -> 50% -> 100%): advance only if rolling 1h windows meet burn-rate and latency stability checks. At 50% and 100% triggers run a regression suite including heavier token-length synthetic traffic to validate long-tail performance and KV cache warmup behavior.

Immediate rollback conditions: sustained error budget burn-rate > 10x for 5 consecutive minutes OR absolute unavailability > 1% in a 5-minute window for Hosted or >0.5% for Dedicated. Any customer-reported P1 with reproducible regression triggers rollback regardless of canary status.
burn_rate_policy: Error budget burn-rate is computed as (observed SLO breaches / allowable breaches) normalized to window. Use RFC 8733-style burn-rate rules: immediate action if 5m burn-rate > threshold, progressive alerts at 10m and 1h.

Thresholds: inform (notify SRE/PM) at 3x burn in 10m, escalate (pause rollout) at 5x burn in 10m, emergency rollback at 10x burn sustained for 5m. For Dedicated, scale thresholds by pool size and per-customer baseline error variance.

Mitigations: when burn-rate thresholds hit, recommended mitigations include traffic-shift to fallback model variant, revert config changes (e.g., batching/quanta change), or scale up reserved capacity for Dedicated. Document chosen mitigation in incident notes.
monitoring_and_alerting: Deliverables before release: a) SLO dashboard (30d rolling, 24h, 1h views) b) burn-rate alarms wired to PagerDuty c) synthetic canary dashboard d) per-region per-model latency heatmap.

Alert definitions: PagerDuty severity mapping: SEV1 for immediate rollback conditions, SEV2 for canary/early-warning thresholds, SEV3 for deviation but non-blocking. Alerts must include runbook links and recent commit/build id used in the canary.

Observability requirements: traces must include token-generation timing, kv-cache hit/miss tags, kernel path selection tag, and request routing decision tag to attribute regressions to routing vs runtime vs model.
acceptance_criteria: Authoritative SLO table committed to runtime-1.20 spec and approved by SRE and Eng leads.
SLI measurement logic implemented in monitoring backend (ENG) with unit and integration tests that validate exclusion rules and percentile calculation approach.
Dashboard and burn-rate alerting defined and running in staging, exerciseable by product and SRE via synthetic canaries.
Rollout gating implemented in Console: automated preflight, staged canary percentages, and auto-abort hooks wired to rollback mechanism. Manual override documented.
Synthetic canary test suite that covers short and long token-length profiles, streaming behavior, and KV cache warmup, with baseline comparisons against previous release measured and stored.
Documentation: operational playbook (runbook) published with step-by-step rollback and customer comms template for P1/P2 incidents tied to SLO breaches.
Security sign-off if private deployment changes SLI export surface (APIs, metrics endpoints).
Stakeholder approvals: SRE, Runtime Eng, Console Eng, Legal (SLA language advisory), and two Customer Success reps for Dedicated/Private customer impact guidance.
test_plan:
Staging job to run full synthetic suite for every candidate build.
- Load profile A: short prompts (<=128 tokens) at 200rps for 30m.
- Load profile B: mixed prompt lengths to exercise long-tail KV behavior for 60m.
- Streaming profile: 100 concurrent streams for 30m with partial chunk delays to validate streaming SLI.
Backfill data: store synthetic run results to help compute expected burn-rate and to serve as baseline for canaries.
User-impact simulation: run chaos test that randomly delays KV cache hits to measure graceful degradation and ensure fallbacks meet acceptance latency thresholds.
notes: Design tradeoffs: we weight p95 for customer-facing SLOs but include p50 as secondary to detect distribution shifts. For Dedicated, tighter availability targets reflect contractual expectations but require per-pool statistical smoothing to avoid false positives. We agreed to start with conservative automatic abort thresholds and loosen as confidence grows. Next step: align with ENG on the exact histogram implementation (hdr vs t-digest) and metric cardinality cost.
decision_records: Decided to exclude 4xx client errors from availability denominator to avoid penalizing client misconfiguration - agreed 2025-01-20 by SRE and PM.
Decided to treat streaming chunk failure as availability breach only if final stream is incomplete - agreed 2025-01-22.
Decided to require synthetic canary run for 30 minutes preflight for every major rollout and 10 minutes for patch builds - agreed 2025-01-28.
